summary: R21 smoke test — Playwright completed all UI checkpoints. All P0 flows PASS. One minor backend defensive-coding issue found where /api/customer/bookings/{id} raises KeyError:'driver_id' when the booking document lacks that field (server.py:2787 and siblings use b['driver_id'] instead of b.get('driver_id')). This did not exist in the R19 seed because that helper explicitly set driver_id=None. R21 QA fix: I added driver_id=None to my seed docs so testing could proceed; recommend main agent switch b['driver_id'] → b.get('driver_id') across GET/messaging/order-detail paths as a hardening fix. Everything else — driver list/map/filters, ASAP inline persistence + nationwide + cancel + audit, recovery vehicle_details rendering, responsive at 390x844 + 1024x800 — all green.

minor.issue: server.py:2787 uses `b['driver_id']` and `user['id'] not in (b['customer_id'], b['driver_id'])` — raises KeyError:'driver_id' → 500 if the booking doc omits the field. Also at lines 2758, 2776, 2798, 2820, 2830. Recommend b.get('driver_id'). Encountered while seeding a paid-unassigned ASAP booking; production booking rows created via legit checkout include driver_id=None so this is only a robustness concern, but the identical seed pattern is what /app/backend/tests/test_final_qa_r19_dispatch_refund.py::_seed_asap_paid uses — that helper DOES set driver_id=None explicitly, which is why R19 tests never tripped this.

rca of the issue: The one backend KeyError encountered is because a customer booking-detail endpoint reads b['driver_id'] unconditionally. Legit checkout inserts driver_id (as None or a value); direct-mongo seeds may omit it. Fix: use .get('driver_id') at server.py lines 2758, 2776, 2787, 2798, 2820, 2830. No customer-visible impact in current codepath because real bookings always have the field, but this is defensive hardening.
